abilities.name: Moonfire
abilities.description: Burns the target with lunar fire over 3 turns.
abilities._source: || Duration 3 -> 4 turns, 6 Nov 2026. Kyle: 'we KNOW rejuv should not be the same duration as regrowth or wild growth etc.' He was right and ours were backwards - Rejuvenation ran 4 turns while Regrowth, the long-tail spell, was tied for SHORTEST at 3, and Wild Growth, the emergency AoE, matched the blanket. Bucket: tail - the dot you open with and leave running. The window is measured, not guessed: tools/sim_class_balance.py plus a boss-multiplier run put trash fights at 2-3 turns (p90 4-5) and boss fights at 5-6 (p90 8-10), so realised damage for a dot applied on turn 1 is 2t 100%, 3t 91%, 4t 78%, 5t 66%, 6t 57% on trash. WoW's RELATIVE ordering is preserved (Wild Growth < Rejuvenation < Regrowth) rather than its absolute seconds, which belong to a game with far longer fights. PER-TICK IS HELD AT THE SHIPPED VALUE and the total scales with duration, because effect_value is the TOTAL across the duration (abilities.py:2695) - moving duration alone would thin a fixed total instead of changing the spell's strength.

abilities.name: Rejuvenation
abilities.description: Nature's energy restores your health over 4 turns.
abilities._source: 29 Oct 2026, Kyle: "Resto druid is designed to be a hot Healer, we need to buff its hots." READ THE INSTRUMENT NOTE IN tools/sim_role_balance.py BEFORE RE-TUNING THIS. The 94-healing-a-turn figure that prompted the request was mostly a measurement fault: the healer sim re-cast the top-priority heal every turn at the same patient, and status_effects refreshes a same-effect_id application, so every HoT was wiped one turn after it landed and credited with a single tick - then divided by casts under a per-turn label. Measured properly the spec was on 182/turn, tenth of thirteen rather than last by 2.5x, and one of only four healers that never runs dry in a 40-turn window. So this is a modest lift into the middle of the field, not the 3x the broken number argued for. Rejuvenation 144 -> 230 (36 -> 57 a turn), Regrowth 117 -> 200 (39 -> 67). Costs follow at 1.42 heal/mana, anchored to priest_renew - the one HoT the game authors above the 1.25 heal/mana constant that Priest Heal, Shaman Healing Wave, Paladin Holy Light and every Sun Cleric, Venomancer, Starcaller, Primalist and Tinker heal sit on. Regrowth was the real defect: at 117 for 135 mana it was on 0.87, BELOW the constant, the only primary-healer heal in the game priced worse than the economy. Healing Touch (134) and Swiftmend left alone on purpose - the spec should stay weakest on burst and strongest on rolling HoTs, which is what makes it read as a different healer from Priest. Durations left at 4 and 3; worth noting they are the shortest HoTs in the field (Venomancer runs 10, 8 and 7, Primalist 8 and 6, Sun Cleric 6) but that is a separate design question. || Duration 4 -> 3 turns, 6 Nov 2026. Kyle: 'we KNOW rejuv should not be the same duration as regrowth or wild growth etc.' He was right and ours were backwards - Rejuvenation ran 4 turns while Regrowth, the long-tail spell, was tied for SHORTEST at 3, and Wild Growth, the emergency AoE, matched the blanket. Bucket: standard - the cheap blanket you keep rolling. The window is measured, not guessed: tools/sim_class_balance.py plus a boss-multiplier run put trash fights at 2-3 turns (p90 4-5) and boss fights at 5-6 (p90 8-10), so realised damage for a dot applied on turn 1 is 2t 100%, 3t 91%, 4t 78%, 5t 66%, 6t 57% on trash. WoW's RELATIVE ordering is preserved (Wild Growth < Rejuvenation < Regrowth) rather than its absolute seconds, which belong to a game with far longer fights. PER-TICK IS HELD AT THE SHIPPED VALUE and the total scales with duration, because effect_value is the TOTAL across the duration (abilities.py:2695) - moving duration alone would thin a fixed total instead of changing the spell's strength.

abilities.name: Swiftmend
abilities.description: Consumes an active Rejuvenation or Regrowth on the target, instantly healing them for the remainder of that effect.
abilities._design_note: Not learned from level alone - granted by the Swiftmend talent in the Restoration tree. Consumes an active Rejuvenation or Regrowth on the target, instantly healing them for the remainder of that effect. Requires one of those to already be active on the target. 29 Oct 2026: consumable_hot_ids listed only druid_rejuvenation, but the ability's own failure message in combat/abilities.py says "requires an active Rejuvenation or Regrowth" and the consumable_hot_ids docstring gives ["druid_rejuvenation", "druid_regrowth"] as its worked example for Swiftmend. The data was the odd one out, so Regrowth was added. effect_value 0 is correct and deliberate - the heal is tick_potency * remaining duration of whatever it eats, so it scales with the Rejuvenation and Regrowth buffs automatically and needs no value of its own.

abilities.name: Thorns
abilities.description: Sheathes the target in thorns, increasing the damage they deal.
abilities._design_note: Real WOTLK Thorns makes enemies who melee the target take Nature damage. This engine has no reflect-damage-on-being-hit mechanic at all, so Thorns has always been an approximation. DEAD UNTIL 2026-10-29, in two ways at once: the stat_mod was {'physical_damage': 0.03}, and (a) 'physical_damage' is not a stat key anything in entities/ or combat/ reads, and (b) the buff branch int()s every non-_pct key, so 0.03 truncated to 0 - the buff landed carrying {'physical_damage': 0}. Two independent reasons for it to do nothing, which is why neither was noticed. Now damage_dealt_pct 3.0, a key the engine really reads (Ability._damage_multiplier) in PERCENT POINTS, so the +3% the old value was evidently reaching for actually applies. STILL AN APPROXIMATION: a real Thorns wants a reflect mechanic, which is Kyle's call and a bigger change than this.

abilities.name: Bear Form
abilities.description: Shapeshift into Bear Form, trading your Mana pool for Rage and increasing Armor and Stamina.
abilities._source: Real castable shapeshift, per Kyle's direction that forms should be actual spells rather than a separate menu (form_screen.py + its H-keybind are being retired). Class-wide baseline per real WoW - any Druid can Bear Form. Uses the existing combat/forms.py 'bear' form data (Lvl 10, Rage resource).

abilities.name: Cat Form
abilities.description: Shapeshift into Cat Form, trading your Mana pool for Energy and increasing Agility and critical strike chance.
abilities._source: Real castable shapeshift, class-wide baseline per real WoW. Uses the existing combat/forms.py 'cat' form data (Lvl 20, Energy resource).

abilities.name: Moonkin Form
abilities.description: Shapeshift into Moonkin Form, increasing Armor and spell critical strike chance.
abilities._source: Real castable shapeshift, unlocked by the Balance capstone talent. Uses the existing combat/forms.py 'moonkin' form data (Lvl 40, Mana resource - no resource change, just stat bonuses). Was previously a fake always-on passive stat bundle rather than a real toggleable form. Gated behind the Balance talent on 6 Nov 2026. The _source note already said 'unlocked by the Balance capstone talent' and druid_balance has carried an unlock_ability node for it all along - requires_talent was simply never set, so the form was auto-learned at 40 and the talent point bought nothing. Confirmed a real talent in 3.3.5a: Balance row 6 (1 rank), so our tier-6 placement is two tiers too deep - the Balance rebuild moves it to tier 4. See data/reference/wotlk_worksheets/druid.md.

abilities.name: Tree of Life
abilities.description: Shapeshift into Tree of Life, increasing healing done and reducing heal-over-time Mana costs.
abilities._source: Real castable shapeshift, unlocked by the Restoration capstone talent. Uses the existing combat/forms.py 'tree_of_life' form data (Lvl 50, Mana resource). Was previously a fake always-on passive stat bundle rather than a real toggleable form. Gated behind the Restoration talent on 6 Nov 2026, same half-finished change as Moonkin Form. Confirmed a real talent in 3.3.5a: Restoration row 8 (1 rank), so it belongs at tier 5; ours sits at tier 3 and stays there because druid_restoration is on Kyle's no-touch list. Only the ability's requires_talent flag changed - the tree is untouched.

abilities.name: Dire Bear Form
abilities.description: Shapeshift into Dire Bear Form, an improved Bear Form with more Armor, Stamina, and Attack Power.
abilities._source: Real castable shapeshift, unlocked by the Feral capstone talent. Uses the existing combat/forms.py 'dire_bear' form data (Lvl 40, Rage resource). Gated behind the Feral talent on 6 Nov 2026. THIS ONE IS A DELIBERATE DEPARTURE FROM REAL WoW: Dire Bear Form is trainer-learned at 40 in 3.3.5a and appears nowhere in the Feral tree. But druid_feral already carries a dire_bear unlock node, and druid_feral is on the no-touch list - so the choice was a live talent that deviates, or a dead 1-point node that matches. A dead node is strictly worse for the player. Gating it costs no edit to the no-touch tree at all.
